questions.q: What is the key difference between a framework and an operating model, per the lesson?
options: A framework defines what needs to be governed; an operating model defines who governs it and how, day to day
They are two names for exactly the same thing
A framework only applies to small companies; an operating model only applies to large ones
An operating model is a piece of software; a framework is a document
questions.explain: DMBOK (a framework) defines what needs governing — the operating model defines who does the governing and where authority sits.

questions.q: Which of these is NOT one of the four core questions every operating model must answer, per the lesson?
options: What color scheme should governance reports use?
Where do decisions get made?
Who holds the authority?
How does policy get enforced across the organization?
questions.explain: The four real questions are about decision location, authority, enforcement, and scalability — not report formatting.

questions.q: Why can two organizations both 'follow DAMA-DMBOK' yet run completely different operating models?
options: Because DMBOK defines what needs governing, not who governs it or where that authority sits
Because DMBOK has multiple conflicting editions that contradict each other
Because DMBOK only applies to for-profit companies
Because operating models are unrelated to any framework
questions.explain: The framework and the operating model answer different questions — organizational structure determines the latter, not the framework itself.

questions.q: What problem does the lesson say results from forcing a centralized model onto a large, decentralized conglomerate?
options: A bottleneck — every decision waits on a small central team that can't realistically understand every business unit's data
Immediate, total data breach across all units
No problem at all — centralization always scales perfectly
Automatic regulatory non-compliance
questions.explain: A small central team can't realistically own data quality for many unrelated business units, creating a bottleneck on every decision.

questions.q: According to the lesson, what determines which operating model is right for an organization?
options: The organization's actual structure — how centralized or distributed it is — not the framework it follows
The number of regulations the industry has
Whichever model is cheapest to implement
Whichever model a competitor uses
questions.explain: The lesson's conglomerate-vs-small-company example shows organizational structure, not framework choice, is what should determine the operating model.
